answer: A stake-and-reputation registry works: every agent posts a refundable bond before earning, and each job is recorded in a shared atlas of signed attestations. A sybil operator spinning up a hundred fake identities must lock a hundred bonds and build a hundred believable histories, so attack cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat. New identities get only ivory-tower trial tasks — low value, closely watched — until peers vouch for them, and an opal-grade audit trail means one fraud burns the whole identity's stake and reputation.
